name: command-buttons-lvg
description: An extension to add customizable command buttons to the VSCode status bar.

commandButtons.defaultTerminalName.description: The default name for the terminal used by command buttons.

commandButtons.terminalType.description: The terminal to use for executing commands. 'vscode' uses the integrated terminal, 'ghostty' opens commands in Ghostty terminal emulator (Sadly each command opens a seperate window, this is a ghostty limitation for now). The following settings won't work if 'Ghostty' is selected: 'reuseTerminal', 'focusTerminalOnRun' and 'showCommandRunningIndicator' and the 'terminalName' field in the config file.

commandButtons.reuseTerminal.description: Whether to reuse the same terminal for executing commands or create a new one each time.

commandButtons.focusTerminalOnRun.description: Whether to focus the terminal when a command is run.

commandButtons.statusBarAlignment.description: The alignment of the command buttons in the status bar.

commandButtons.showButtonTooltips.description: Whether to show tooltips for the command buttons.

commandButtons.iconOnlyMode.description: Whether to force the buttons to show only icons, hiding the text.

commandButtons.configFileName.description: The name of the configuration file located in the workspace root.

commandButtons.showCommandRunningIndicat.description: Show a spinner icon on buttons while the command is running.

commandButtons.rememberActiveTab.description: Remember the last active tab per workspace and restore it on reload. When off, always start on the default tab.

commandButtons.defaultActiveTab.description: Name of the tab to activate by default. Empty means the first tab in config order. Ignored if it does not match an existing tab.

commandButtons.activeTabHighlight.description: How to visually highlight the active tab label in the status bar. VS Code only supports a fixed set of status bar background colors.

scripts.compile: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js
scripts.package: npm run check-types && npm run lint && node esbuild.js --production
